_comment: Maintained by Claude — see ../CLAUDE.md 'Dashboard Maintenance' rule. Status values: concept | in-progress | review | ready | archived. Keys in 'mocks' are folder paths relative to products/Scheduling/ (no trailing /index.html).

recentChanges.summary: Renamed 'CrewSense' to 'Crew Scheduler' in the CallBack Methodology step ('Crew Scheduler sends the call') across both the Rules engine prototype and the test mock — aligns labeling with current product naming.

Rule builder + Preview Mode overhaul: swapped the '+' glyph to a sparkles icon on every 'Add new rule' surface; hide the sub-sidebar when the rule builder owns the screen (focus mode); fixed A&R page-level scrolling (removed the inner card's overflow:hidden trap); all configurable fields now render on the right-side panel from the start with the same highlight pulse when chat fills them in. Chat now answers 'What is <rule type>?' inline with an AI tutor explanation; 'Save rule' / 'Preview ranking' / 'Adjust something' end-of-flow chips are wired to commit/save, jump into Preview, and ask 'What would you like to change?' with the change-menu chips. A Preview Mode button appears in the builder header once minimum info is in. Preview Mode now shows a horizontal stepper for the callback chain (#1 → #N) and the per-step 'System decides / Someone else accepted' radios collapsed into a single dropdown — 'Random (system decides)' as the first option, followed by every available person. Sim chat auto-scrolls to the latest AI answer.

Approaches & Rules polish + Save Rule routing: CallBack Methodology accordion now starts open so users land on the page already oriented. Save Rule no longer renders an inline 'Rule saved!' confirmation screen — instead it routes the user back to Approaches & Rules, pushes the new rule to the TOP of the rules list with a green 'NEW' badge alongside the AI badge, and shows a green dismissable toast banner ('Rule saved — X has been added to your rules list') at the top of the page that auto-dismisses after ~4.5s. Editing an existing rule produces the same flow with 'Rule updated' wording. Also removed the floating GitHub Pages share pill from this mock per stakeholder request.

Rule edit + Preview Mode polish: randomized Preview Mode's auto-simulate (variable decline counts) and seeded the predicted-ranking with a per-reset jitter so the order visibly shakes on each reset; preview chat now opens with a quick rule summary; removed the Online pill in the scenario-assistant header; added ~320px scroll headroom below both the rule-builder config panel and the Preview Mode form so dropdowns near the bottom don't clip. Edit-rule chat now drops the 'Welcome back' line and orange 'Editing: X' banner and leads with 'This is the rule you pulled up' + summary; the configuration panel starts collapsed and opens when the user picks 'Let's change something'. Edit chips now mix exploratory ('Why is X first?', 'How many hours does X have?', 'Where is X in the ranking?') with the change/save options.

Preview Mode: replaced the full-width Scenario Assistant banner with a chatbot-style card pinned to the top of the left column, directly above 'Choose CallBack Shift date / time'. Card has a real chat header (purple gradient, AI avatar, Online dot), scrollable thread, quick-prompt chips, and an input row at the bottom — reads as a chatbot rather than a generic banner. The predicted-call-order column on the right now naturally moves up to fill the space the banner used to occupy.

Lengthened every rule-type FLOWS path so the chat covers the operational settings the real Vector Scheduling rule form exposes — not just 4 quick questions. Each flow now asks (after the rule-type-specific core) a tail of common questions: shift-length filter, callback statuses (multi-select), callback responses (multi-select), 'include previously created shifts' toggle, and (for Rolodex types) 'Rule evaluates: Callbacks only / All shifts'. Hours-Based also asks lookback + forecast windows. Added two new form fields (ruleEvaluates, includePrevShifts), new extractAnswer matches for the new chip values, and new right-panel sections so the answers light up live as you chat.

When the user clicks an existing rule to edit it, the AI's opening message now describes the current configuration in plain English ('This is a Standard Rolodex rule, applied to Bay Guard. After accepting a callback, employees are moved to end of list, and each has 3 minutes to respond…') instead of dumping a bullet-list of field values. Implementation: rewrote summarizeRule() to build natural sentences keyed off rule-type-specific fields (post-accept move + response window for Rolodex, accumulation type + rotation limit for Accumulating Rolodex, reset cadence + outcomes counted for hours/turns, tiebreaker, decline behavior).

Reworded the AI rule-builders' first question from 'Which group(s) should this rule apply to?' to 'Which approach(es) should this rule apply to?' on both surfaces (dashboard AIAssistantCard + Approaches & Rules banner) and in the in-chat 'Change groups' follow-up, so terminology matches the underlying Approaches data model.

Rule Configuration panel field order now matches the new chat sequence: Rule Name → Rule Affects (+ embedded selected-approach chips for the people group) → Rule Type → per-rule-type follow-ups. Previously Rule Type appeared right after Rule Name and Rule Affects sat at the bottom; since groups are now pre-picked upstream and the rule-type question comes after, the panel reads top-to-bottom in the same order the user answers.

Rule-builder dual-screen first question (the rule-type picker, reached from both the dashboard AIAssistantCard and the Approaches & Rules banner): replaced the standalone card-style suggestions with light-purple chip bubbles matching the rest of the in-chat single-select questions, flattened the two paginated SUGGESTION_SETS so all six rule types show at once, removed the 'Show more suggestions / Back to first suggestions' rotator, and added the standard 'Something else' (custom answer) and 'Skip for now' affordances so the first step feels consistent with later steps.

Dashboard AIAssistantCard freeform input now uses the highlighted/glowing treatment (pencil icon, purple tinted gradient background, glow ring, on-focus brightening) — same style already used by the Approaches & Rules banner input — so users notice they can write a rule freehand alongside the chips.

Unified the two AI rule-builder entry surfaces (dashboard AIAssistantCard + Approaches & Rules 'Add new rule' banner): replaced the purple 'Callback Ranking Rules Engine / Build intelligent callback rules with AI' header with a clean '+ Add new rule' title, moved the 'Which group(s) should this rule apply to?' subheader onto its own line, added a 'PICK ONE OR MORE' gray uppercase helper above the chips, shifted the 'Select all / Clear all' toggle below the chips, and removed the empty-state 'Pick at least one group to continue' button so the Continue CTA only appears once a group is selected. Also renamed the rule-builder dual-screen page header from '+ Create new rule' to '+ Add new rule' (in both prototypes) for consistency.

Rule Configuration panel: hoisted the 'Next: [employee name]' indicator out of the Preview Ranking / Rule Summary tab strip and placed it next to the Collapse Panel button in the panel's sticky header so it stays visible on every tab. Removed the small sparkle/AI icon from the tab strip (and the duplicate '1st [name]' chip from the collapsed Rule Summary pill) to reclaim horizontal room inside the summary box.

Rules Engine: restyled the shared GroupPickerChips component (used by both the dashboard AI assistant card and the Approaches & Rules 'Add New Rule' banner) as add/remove badges — default state shows a leading '+' icon and outlined pill, selected state shows a filled purple bubble with a trailing 'x' to deselect.

Rules Engine + AI search engine dashboard: changed the AI rule-builder header to '+ Create new rule' (removed the 'Build intelligent callback rules with AI' subtitle) and reworked the chat's group multi-select from chip bubbles into a horizontal row of checkboxes with a leading 'Select all' option for clearer affordance.

Rules Engine: dashboard + Approaches & Rules AI cards now start with a multi-select group picker (Firefighter 2, Captains, Patrol Deputy, Bay Guard, Battalion Chief, FF3, Select all) instead of rule-type prompts. Selected groups carry into the rule builder so it skips the 'Which group?' question. Existing rules in the Rules list are now clickable to edit — opening a rule pre-fills every config field on the right panel and the chat starts with a configuration summary + change-this-field chips (Change groups, Change tiebreaker, Change reset cadence, Change decline behavior, All good — save). The right-panel config now glows on the most recently revealed field after each chat answer so users notice fresh additions. Also removed Michael Only from APPROACHES_DATA.
Approaches & Rules is now the default landing view for the Rules Engine prototype (was Dashboard).

Preview Mode button now opens a full simulation modal (not just a visual toggle). The modal shows: a hypothetical scenario card (overtime fire watch, 12-hour sick relief, mutual-aid standby — cyclable), the predicted call order computed from the in-progress rule, a two-step dispatch flow (decline → next person accepts) that reflects the rule's decline-action setting, and an 'Ask the AI a specific scenario' panel with sample question chips ('What if the top 3 decline?', tie handling, fiscal reset, PTO) plus a freeform input. AI answers are generated by a local pattern matcher that consults the user's actual rule fields, so the preview feels rule-aware.

Added a Preview Mode toggle button to the top-right of the rule-builder dual-screen header banner. Hovering it reveals a dark tooltip describing the tool ('Optional exercise for all rule activations and edits. Simulates ranking outcomes before go-live. For customers with no historical data, the system provides generic, appropriate hypothetical scenarios. The customer can also ask the AI chat how the rule would handle specific scenarios that they provide.'). Clicking flips the button to an inverted white/purple 'ON' state so users can see they're in preview mode.

Rule Type dropdown in the right-panel config now mirrors the six prompt names (Standard Rolodex, Accumulating Rolodex, Accumulation — Hours Based, Static — Seniority Based, Static — By Employee ID, Random / Lottery, Custom) so the selected option matches the card the user clicked. Restructured the panel so the Rule Summary / Preview Ranking lives inside the scroll area with position:sticky — it scrolls up with content and a scroll listener auto-collapses it into a compact pill once you scroll past 36px (re-expands near the top), freeing vertical room on a laptop. Added per-prompt call-and-response fields (post-accept move + response window, accumulation type + limit, reset cadence + outcomes counted, seniority date type, sort direction + new-hire placement + case handling, randomize frequency + weighting + guardrail) so answering chat chips reveals new fields on the right.
